articles.title: “THE VOICE OF THE SON OF GOD”
articles.author: C. F. Dadd

paragraphs.text: The thought in reading these few verses is to draw our attention to the voice of the Son of God. We would, as our brother has said in prayer, desire to hear what the Lord would say to us as we are together. What might proceed here today as to the voice of the Son of God being heard, the word of the Lord coming in, would be directed to “we, the living, who remain” (1

Thessalonians 4: 15). Our brother’s testimony here is finished. His days have been long in the land, but now it is for “we who remain” and what proceeds now would be in relation to ourselves. The Lord intends that His voice might be a known thing amongst us. We are thankful for the fact that with most, if not all, the voice of the Son of God has been heard in our own private histories. This is true as we have known what it is to accept Christ. He said,

“I say unto you, that an hour is coming, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God”. What a marvellous thing it is that the voice of the Son of God has been heard, possibly in the experience of every one of us, appealing to us as to where we have been in our own lives before God, because the Lord said, “the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God”. We are not thinking that He said that of the physical dead. He is thinking of those who are away from God, that do not know Christ. Today we are within the range of the voice of the Son of God and we are to know what it is to live. So God

would appeal to us. Our brother was long in the enjoyment of this, and now it is a question of ourselves. In prayer reference was made to “we, the living”, and what a voice things are now to us, “we, the living, who remain”.
Our brother has been gently and graciously put to sleep by Jesus. Paul speaks about that—

those who are asleep through Jesus. The Lord has been the One by whom our brother has been put to sleep. But we who remain are still in the sphere of responsibility. We are still in the sphere where we have to do with God, where we have to do with the Son of God, so that His voice would be heard at such a time as this, and that those who hear shall live. How important is what John has to say in his gospel; how it bears so much on the desire that we might have life. What a great matter that is; life from a moral viewpoint. Life for the believer is the power to enjoy what God has brought him within the range of. That is the idea of life—
the power to enjoy what God has provided. What a test it is as to our place in the testimony at this time.

In verse 28 the Lord speaks about the time that is coming when “all who are in the tombs shall hear his voice”. That takes us on to a further thought to those that have died in Christ; those that have died generally, too. Every man, woman and child that has ever lived will be raised by the voice of the Son of God. Those that are in the tombs shall hear His voice. Think of the resurrection soon to take place, how private and personal it will be for those who believe—like the resurrection of Lazarus, where the Lord said, “Lazarus, come forth” (John 11: 43), and he came forth. That will proceed, with every one who believes; there is going to be the resurrection of the just. It speaks here of the resurrection of life, as it shall be, according to the faith of our
brother who has departed to be with Christ.

How the gospel, how the word of God, how the voice of the Son of God, come within our range at a moment such as this and it would be that we might come into the area of life, enjoying what it is to be quickened by that voice, made to live to God. Paul could speak about that, that if he lived in the flesh, he lived according to his faith in the Son of God.

I would leave this with each one of us now, that the voice of the Son of God, to be heard so vividly at a moment such as this, might enter into the hearts of every one of us and affect us, so that the time we have left might be committed to be here for His pleasure. May it be so.

These scriptures would indicate the Lord’s interest in each one of us. The first part of the book convinces you of that. He knows all about us as He repeats “I know”, “I know”, “I know”. Our dear sister, whom we desire to be comforted, can take courage from that. The Lord in John 11 refers to Lazarus as “our friend”—“Lazarus, our friend, is fallen asleep, but I go that I may awaken him out of sleep”. What consideration! Arriving at the house, His word of comfort to Martha was, “Thy brother shall rise again”. Our dear sister can take comfort that our brother shall rise again.

What I want to call attention to in a simple way is how the Lord takes account of faithfulness on the part of His people, and rightly appraises features found in them. Perhaps I should not use the word ‘rightly’, for could the Lord’s action in any respect be other than right?
Whatever He said or did was not simply right but perfect, and could not be improved upon.

The point I am emphasising is the manner in which He values faithfulness in any of us. Verse 13 of the chapter reads, “I know where thou dwellest, where the throne of Satan is”. Think of that! Our sister need not fear. The Lord is able for every situation that might confront us.

Then, “Thou holdest fast my name, and hast not denied my faith, even in the days in which Antipas my faithful witness was, who was slain among you, where Satan dwells”. He is speaking of a local brother in Pergamos. What a privilege to be among such persons in whom the Lord takes such interest! It is affecting how the apostles speak of the Lord’s sojourn here in manhood. Peter refers touchingly to “all the time in which the Lord Jesus came in and went out among us”, Acts 1: 21. John says “The Word became flesh, and dwelt among us”, John 1: 14. What impressions these apostles received; what experiences they acquired from the Lord’s movements and presence among them! He Himself as among them said, “I am in the midst of you as the one that serves”, Luke 22: 27. What a service it was!

But my point now is Antipas to whom the Lord refers as “my faithful witness”. This is challenging to all of us, as to whether the Lord can regard us in our localities as faithful persons. He knows all the conditions and circumstances with which we have to contend. He knows us, too, and His eye is upon us. He, the faithful and true Witness, has left an area in which His lovers can be faithful to Him in His absence. “My faithful witness”—what a

commendation this is of Antipas who was slain as a result of his steadfastness! Our brother has not been slain among us, thank God. In the mercy of God conditions are not so extreme as yet, but such were the conditions in Pergamos. The Lord has promised to keep His own out of the hour of trial which is about to come upon the whole habitable world, and we can be comforted in that promise.

I trust we will be encouraged in this line of faithfulness. Our brother, who had his own place in the locality, has served his generation and has fallen asleep. He has finished his course, I think with joy, too. Who is going to fill the vacancy? Paul speaks of being “baptised for the dead”, 1 Corinthians 15: 29. This expression means, to give a military application, that as soon as one soldier is struck down another immediately steps forward in his place in the rank.

So Peter in Acts 1, already referred to, said it was necessary to appoint one from among them to take the place of Judas. I am not suggesting that the brethren choose anyone, of course. At the same time, inasmuch as responsibility has to be assumed in a locality, there must be one to take it on. I am thinking rather on individual lines, that where there is a need some individual instinctively seeks grace to supply the need. May the Lord bless the word.

articles.title: GOD IS NOT GOD OF THE DEAD BUT OF THE LIVING
articles.author: A. B. Parker
articles.place: Words at the burial of Mr, P. W. Coombs, Plainfield, N.J.

paragraphs.text: This scripture was used by the Lord Jesus in meeting the Sadducees’ attack on the truth of

resurrection. He said to them, “But that the dead rise, even Moses shewed … when he called the Lord the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob”, adding, “but he is not God of the dead but of the living”, Luke 20: 37, 38.

These three men were representative persons. God is said to be the God of others, too—“All these died in faith … wherefore God is not ashamed of them, to be called their God”, Hebrews 11: 13–16. But we know the histories of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Abraham was a man of faith; he “believed God”, Romans 4: 3. Our dear brother was also a man of faith; he believed God; he lived by faith, and he died in faith. I have no hesitation in saying that God is not ashamed of him to be called his God.

Isaac enjoyed a peculiar place in sonship. Abraham was told, “Take now thy son, thine only son, whom thou lovest, Isaac …”, Genesis 22: 2. And later, Abraham gave gifts to the sons of his concubines and sent them away from Isaac (Genesis 25: 6) that there should be no rival to Isaac, the only son of the free woman. It is a wonderful thing to have a sense of the Father’s love for His sons, so distinctly and uniquely set out in Christ, the only-begotten, but entered into by us through adoption, having received “a spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father”, Romans.8: 15. Our brother knew the blessed liberty of sonship.

Jacob is well known to most of us and much could be said about him, but I wish to be brief, so I will refer to what, possibly, was one of the most important experiences in the life of Jacob. When he came to Bethel, according to Genesis 35: 7, “He built there an altar, and called the place El-Beth-el”, meaning God of the house of God. He worshipped the God of the house of God! The

apostle Paul tells us that in this dispensation the saints are “built together for a habitation of God in the Spirit”, Ephesians 2: 22. We are free to worship the Spirit of God. There are some believers who are not. Our brother was one who worshipped the Spirit of God, recognizing His place in Deity.

These distinctive features to which we have referred were seen outstandingly, in representation, in the three men of whom God said, “I am the God … of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob”. They all were in their graves when God said that to Moses, but they were living for God, for “he is not God of the dead but of the living”. Our brother has died, but he is living for God. He has departed to be with Christ, of which Paul could say, “It is very much better”, Philippians 1: 23. He is living for God in conditions where faith no longer is needed, for things which he held in faith he now enjoys in reality; acceptance in sonship is now unhindered, and God is worshipped without let. And God is not ashamed of him to be called his God.

It is very interesting to see what God secures at the end of the dispensations. In the time before the flood God had Noah, one who was “a just man, perfect amongst his generations”, a man, who “walked with God”, Genesis 6: 9. That dispensation did not finish without God having something. In the end of Malachi we are told of those that feared Jehovah and spoke often one to another, and thought upon His name (Malachi 3: 16).

It is quite clear that that dispensation did not finish without some spoil for God. So in the one in which we are the finish will see something for God according to His own mind, according to His own thoughts; there will be persons waiting for the Lord to come, those who will be suitable to Himself.

So I have read these verses particularly having in mind what the Lord says about John, “If I will that he abide until I come, what is that to thee?”. Now I know that John being spoken of in this way may carry some reference to his ministry, what the Lord gave John to continue, and that particular line of ministry has a very clear bearing on how things will continue till the end of the dispensation, how faith will be sustained in the gain of that. When the Lord comes He will have persons who are going on with the light that has been presented as to these wonderful things that lie in the realm of life and love. But along with that John is a sample of the kind of person that the Lord will have—“If I will that he abide until I come”.

Now there are four things said of John that I want to speak of because they would enter into the constitution of persons who continue until the Lord comes. One is that he was the disciple whom Jesus loved; another is that he is following; then that he leaned at supper on His breast; and the fourth is that he said, “Lord, who is it that delivers thee up?”, that is, he had a spirit of enquiry. I just want to enlarge on these things in order to see how we may come into the gain of them for ourselves; that is, they should not merely be things said about John, but things that are true of us. There is nothing in these things that are said about John that any of us should be excluded from. In fact, when John is referring to himself in this way he does not exactly say, ‘I was the disciple whom Jesus loved’, he just refers to “the disciple whom Jesus loved”—he leaves him unnamed, and therefore you can see the possibility immediately of any believer coming into that.

I would like to mention this matter of following, because the Lord is speaking to Peter here and He is saying, “Follow me”. Then Peter turns round and looks at John—is not that just like ourselves? We turn round to see what So-and-so is doing. But the point is that you are to get your eye on the Lord. John did not have to be told to follow, he was already following.

Peter was being instructed to follow, and the Lord has to be emphatic with him, “Follow thou me”. Do not worry about John; he will be all right because he is following. If there is somebody who is following the Lord, he is all right, he will be safe. But the Lord is working with Peter to get him into the same situation as John was already in.

Now the Lord is very interested in persons who want to follow Him. You will remember that there were two of John the baptist’s disciples who heard John speaking about Jesus—a very brief word it was, “Behold the Lamb of God”, and it says they “followed Jesus”, John 1: 36, 37. Now that is a great result from a brother’s ministry, that someone should not just follow the person who gave the word, but that they should follow Christ. That is the point in ministry. If it does not lead us to Christ then it has not fulfilled its objective. But John’s word was immediately effective and they “followed Jesus”. And He saw them following. It is a great matter, you know, to come under the attention of

Jesus; each one of us can come under His personal attention. If He sees us wanting to follow, then He might say what He said to those two, “What seek ye?”. They answered, “Where abidest thou?”. They wanted to see where He lived, His dwelling conditions, and He took those two on “and they abode with him that day”. That must have been a wonderful day, a day with Jesus. Well, He was interested in seeing persons who wanted to follow, and He took them on. You know, the Lord will take us on—and what a vista is open to us in divine things.
Well, there you have persons who are on the line of following.

Now John enlarges on this line in his gospel. In chapter 10, for example, we get the relations between the Shepherd and His sheep, the Lord presenting Himself in that way, “My sheep hear my voice … and they follow me” (John 10: 27). How simple! How attractive! It is what the Person has become to us. What has Jesus become personally to us, dear brethren?

Christianity without Christ is worthless. So it is, “My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me; and I give them life eternal”. It is a fine thing to be able to follow the Lord by hearing His voice. We do not see Him by actual sight, but I think we know something about His voice. Blind people depend a great deal on being able to distinguish persons by their voices. It is very remarkable how acute their power of discernment is. Now is it like that with us, dear brethren? Do we hear a voice and can we say, ‘That is the Lord; that is the Shepherd’s voice’? I think we are to become characteristically persons like that, able to detect the Lord by His voice. I am sure His voice is heard amongst us, dear brethren.
We know His voice and, therefore, we follow Him. Oh the arrangement is so simple!

Oh the things He is wanting to lead us into, dear brethren—life eternal, into this area where we are not affected by the pressure of death. The effect of death is all around, but the Lord would say, ‘I lead my sheep into an area where they can be free from that’. Free from pressure, free even from the pressure of death, the greatest pressure that can be on the human spirit; and the Lord would say, ‘I will lead you into an area where you can be free for God’.

Well, that is what He is doing with persons who hear His voice. He says, “I lay down my life for the sheep”, John 10: 15. That is how He has proved His love. How thankful we should be to be amongst His sheep, those of whom He says, “I am come that they might have life, and might have it abundantly”, John 10: 10. People have a mistaken idea that if they go in for Christ and His things they will be losers, by giving up life in the world. Well, that is a poor kind of life anyway. The kind of life that the Lord wants to impart is life abundantly, a life that never takes anything away from us, that is always on the line of giving, of supply. You get an impression of the wonderful resources that lie behind what the Lord says, and, you know, we need never be at a loss because the shepherd, according to the illustration that the Lord was using, always went before the sheep. And all the way that we are led down here He has gone before, every step of it. “My sheep … follow me”, John 10: 27. They will not follow strangers, He says, “because they know not the voice of strangers” (verse 5). That is, you are able to distinguish. We have to habituate ourselves to this idea of being able to discern between the voice of the Shepherd, and the voice of a stranger.
Now another thing He says is, “If any one serve me, let him follow me; and where I am, there also shall be my servant”, John 12: 26. Well, that

is a good thought to have, to serve Christ, to be serviceable to the Master, but do not let us serve, dear brethren, without Christ. He has to lead you in it and then you can be safe in following. The point is—‘Where I am, there also shall be my servant’. If you are going to serve Christ, you want to be where He is. It is a matter of detecting where He is, following Him and being with Him where He is. It is a question of what He is doing, then we come in and follow Him and find we are serviceable as we follow. Well, John had got the benefit of these things he is portraying in his gospel and represents them in himself as one who was following.

Then he is “the disciple whom Jesus loved”. Now, that is open to us. In John 13 we are told how the Lord washed the disciples’ feet. That was the service of His love towards them; he went round to each of them in turn, then, after that. He has John in His bosom. John understood the affection of Christ. He lay there at supper in the bosom of Jesus. Now that is open to us, dear brethren. You get right to the heart of things in christianity in the bosom of Jesus. We must not say that was for John alone. I think it represents what is open to each one of us to find our place, you might say, just nestling in the love of Christ. If we are amongst those who are to be abiding until He comes, it is to be known by us, what it is to relax in the atmosphere of the love of Christ, to be in His bosom. Jesus is in the bosom of the Father. “No one has seen God at any time”, John tells us, “the only-begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him”, John 1: 18. That is, the whole declaration of God is characterised by a Man in the bosom of the Father. Wonderful!
Therefore we are to understand something of

what the bosom of Jesus means. The Lord’s supper gives us an opportunity for that, when we can just relax in the sense of the love of Christ. That is, you are not occupied with anything else but just Himself and His love. What a thing it is just to take time to enjoy the love of Christ for its own sake. John understood that and would make it attractive to us. He was also a trustworthy person. At the cross Jesus saw the disciple whom He loved and committed His mother to him, indicating that such a one would be trustworthy. Then John was interested when Mary of Magdala came and saw the stone rolled away at the tomb. She came and told Peter and the disciple whom Jesus loved, someone who would be interested in anything that pertained to the Person of Christ.

John 21 is probably the last chapter to be written in the Scriptures, and it is a recovery chapter. It is a man who had known something of recovery who is being spoken of in this way, with the possibility of abiding until the Lord comes. Is that not wonderful encouragement for ourselves? We no longer speak of the recovery as if it were something apart from ourselves; we have had to prove in experience what it is to be recovered and as recovered persons there is the possibility of abiding here until the Lord comes. Just think of that, the privilege that is open to us, not as those who had never departed at all, but as recovered persons. That is what John is here; that is what Peter is, because there had been a departure at the beginning of this chapter. Peter says, “I go to fish” (John 21: 3) and the others say, “We also come with thee”, and then the Lord has to recover them. And who was the means of recovery? The disciple whom Jesus loved. The Lord, of course, effected the recovery, but John discerned Him. He says, “It is the Lord”, and Peter heard that and

moved. Others were affected that way. Someone is able to say, ‘It is the Lord’, and just think of the possibility of someone else being affected and being recovered. John became the means of Peter being recovered because he was able to say, “It is the Lord”, and I think he was able to say that as a result of being the disciple whom Jesus loved.

Dear brethren, this chapter is wonderful encouragement for us to think of recovery. We can think of it as to ourselves. What are we? Recovered persons, and the Lord is continuing to work in recovery. I think we should continue to look to Him for recovery. He has in mind these hundred and fifty-three great fishes, spiritual personalities being recovered. Just think of what the Lord will have in the way of recovery. I do not think it indicates any great public change, but it is how persons are being recovered, persons who can be numbered. It says of Reuben, ‘let his men be easily counted’ (Deuteronomy 33: 6, note)—such as can be numbered, and available to be here till the Lord comes. Well, this is what sustains someone who understands what it is to have a place in the affections of Christ, “the disciple whom Jesus loved”.

Then he “also leaned at supper on his breast”. Now that is a little different from being in His bosom. In His bosom, I think, is how you can relax in the sense of His love, but to lean on His breast means that you prove something of the support of the love of Christ. And we need that. The situation in John 13 was the time when the Lord said, “One of you shall deliver me up” (John 13: 21). You can understand in a situation like that how a sense of the Lord’s support would be needed. John felt that, and he filled out that position as leaning on the breast of Jesus. There are positions in the testimony where we need the consciousness of the

support of the love of Christ—difficult testimonial circumstances. We think of assembly exercises, perhaps household exercises, and as we feel them pressing in upon us we feel the conscious need of the support of the love of Christ. Well, the Lord would afford us that.

I was thinking of Paul in Romans 8 where he says, “Who shall separate us from the love of Christ?”. He says, “We have been reckoned as sheep for slaughter”—difficult, trying, testimonial circumstances—but he says, “In all these things we more than conquer through him that has loved us”. That is, in the knowledge of the supporting love of Christ he is able to go through triumphantly, buoyantly. You cannot do that apart from the support of Christ, leaning on His breast—that is the idea, that you are proving the consciousness of His support.

The same man says, as to the time when all deserted him, “No man stood with me”, but then he says, “The Lord stood with me, and gave me power”, 2 Timothy 4: 16, 17. Think of a man having to stand in the presence of the representatives of all the power of the Roman empire.

How could he do it apart from the consciousness of the support of the love of Christ? Well, that is to be known by us, dear brethren. John himself, in the beginning of Revelation, when the Lord was coming in judicially in the presence of the public breakdown of the assembly, says, “He laid his right hand upon me, saying, Fear not” (Revelation 1: 17)—what a touch!
Oh the supporting power of the love of Christ in difficult circumstances in the testimony, dear brethren! Well, that is to be known by us.
The other thing is that John had said, “Lord, who is it that delivers thee up?”. Peter did not ask this question; Peter made a sign and John asked the question. Now what we ought to be
exercised about is to be able to go to the Lord with an enquiry and ask of Him; to be able to do that ourselves, not to depend on somebody else doing it. That was a difficult situation—

the Lord in John 13 had said, “One of you shall deliver me up”, and John asks, “Lord, who is it?” (verse 25). The Lord did not name him, but indicated how they would know. The Lord may not give us the complete answer immediately, but would give us an indication that should lead us to understand what His mind is. As He proceeded it would become obvious, but we have to follow step by step to reach what the Lord is indicating. Now, dear brethren, I think this is very important in regard to exercises that occur in the testimony—in our localities or in a wider way; what even might occur in the whole area of Christendom that affects the name of Christ—that we might have this enquiring attitude and seek to have understanding of the Lord’s mind so as to be with Him sympathetically.

As we learn what His mind is about things it preserves us from being self-sufficient, from assuming to know everything. The Lord knows everything; He can say, “I know”. Well, we would want to be in the secret of His mind. If He knows, He has all the answers, dear brethren: He has the answers to things that may affect us in our localities, and to things that may affect the saints universally. He would say, “I know”; but He is looking for persons who will be sufficiently interested to seek Him, to seek to understand what His mind is. Well, that is open to us too. John was in that position of being near enough to the Lord to enquire. O, dear brethren, would that we had the exercise to be near enough to the Lord just to enquire and understand what His mind is about matters. He might show us that patience is needed; patience is needed in the working out of things.
That is a great matter. The Lord is working something out and He says of one assembly,

“Thou hast kept the word of my patience”, Revelation 3: 10. Think of God working out the whole dispensation on the principle of long-suffering towards men; what patience is being exercised from the divine side! The Lord Jesus Himself is patiently waiting to have the assembly with Himself—He is waiting for that moment, and we can be sympathetically with Him in seeking to keep the word of His patience, exercised just to go on until what He has in mind is worked out, and seeking to be with Him in some secret understanding of what His mind is.
Well, may the Lord encourage us, dear brethren, to set ourselves to take on these features.

They are compressed just into one verse, you might say, to give us a view of a sample of the kind of believers that He will have when He comes. May we seek to be found amongst them, for His name’s sake.

These words of the Lord Jesus in Luke 11: 23 challenge us as to where we stand in relation to Him in the sphere of testimony, for we are either with Him or we are not. There is no neutral position. This is the time of Christ’s rejection and being with Him involves sacrifice, surrender, and suffering here, but it is where His true lovers are to be
found, and it is the only place of safety, as David (precious type of Christ in rejection) says,
“Abide with me, fear not … for with me thou art in safe keeping”, 1 Samuel 22: 23.

The Lord has great regard for those who are with Him thus as He feelingly says here in Luke 22: 28, “Ye are they who have persevered with me in my temptations”. The reproach and the shame is His, the reproach of the Christ. Our part is to be fully with Him in it, bearing His reproach. The Lord’s use of the word ‘persevere’ shows that it is by no means an easy path, it has many tests, but those who persevere with Him in it are a present comfort to the heart of Christ. The time of His rejection will soon be over. Very soon the once—and still—despised Jesus will appear and the whole earth will be filled with His glory. In the very scene where He was so shamefully treated and where He has long been denied His rights, He will be publicly honoured and vindicated—Lord, be it soon! Faithfulness to Him now will be rewarded then, for those who suffer with Him will be glorified with Him (Romans 8: 17). We might, in a measure of faithfulness, suffer for Him now, but to suffer with Him means that we are unreservedly identified with Him in the reproach linked with the testimonial position at the present time. We shall reign with Him, but what true lovers cherish in their souls is not just the reigning but the blessed prospect of simply being with Him, as Mr. Darby says in one of his choice hymns—
‘But glory on high. Lord,
Is not like being nigh,
When all is gone by, at Thy coming again’.
There is no doubt whatever as to where the malefactor stood in relation to Christ, the holy Sufferer. He was with Him. I admire the moral

courage of that lone man as he confessed the Lord in the presence of the greatest concentration of wickedness and hatred that this world has ever known. He asked to be remembered by the Lord in His kingdom, but what an answer he got! “Today shalt thou be with me in paradise”. To apply this, as we are fully with the Lord Jesus sufferingly in the testimony, we do not have to await His appearing for recompense. There is present recompense each time we assemble for, in the power of the same Spirit who has sustained us in the testimony, we can enter by the opened heavenly door and experience the unspeakable joy of being with Christ in that scene of which He is the glorious centre. As Mr. Raven says, ‘It is the height of grace to be Christ’s companion in the place of supreme bliss’ (N.S. Vol. 9. p.19). May the Holy Spirit be pleased to use these remarks to encourage each one of us to be fully with the Lord Jesus in the testimony in the little time that remains.
Our hearts rejoice afresh, O Lord, to sense
The present ardour of Thy love that leaps
Upon the hills, itself to recompense;
As one who from His own love’s sowing reaps.
Thy love is constant, too, and it has shown
That nothing could its suff’ring course impede—
Nay! rather did it choose to go alone
To death itself—for thus was sown the seed.
The precious grain must fall into the ground
And die, unless it should alone abide.
Now from Thy sowing is a harvest found,
Much fruit—the Son of man thus glorified.
With joy will all the sheaves be gathered now
In resurrection’s field where, as is due,
To Thee the First of first-fruits all do bow—
Yet they through heavenly purpose first-fruits too!
Then harvest must be to the garner brought;
Thy garner, region of ascended life—
Th’assembly by the Spirit’s power inwrought,
Thy bride, Thy body, and Thy cherished wife.
London.

ANOTHER DAY What a wonderful thing each new day is! Another day in which to commit ourselves to the will of God, and in which to have the high privilege of prayer, and communion with Him. A fresh day to praise Him for all His grace and mercy. Another day in which He may have pleasure in our lives, and some fruit and fragrance from them. Another day in which the life of Jesus can be manifested in the lives of His own, affording comfort to the saints and testimony to men. Another day in which to learn more of Christ and all that centres in Him, and to be formed by it. Another day to take up the usual routines and responsibilities—‘The daily round, the common task’—and to carry them out as to the Lord, so that there is a yield to Him from it. Another day to be conscious of a thousand mercies from a Father’s hand, and joyfully
to thank Him for them, and, if there be chastening and affliction, to experience in them the tenderness of our Father’s faithful love, the grace of our Lord Jesus, and the Holy Spirit’s comfort.

The slippery path of sin is always trodden with accelerated steps, because the first sin tends to weaken in the soul the authority and power of that which alone can prevent our committing still greater sins—that is, the word of God, as well as the consciousness of His presence, which imparts to the word all its practical power over us.
paragraphs.source: J. N. Darby (‘Synopsis’ on 1 Kings 10 and 11)

paragraphs.text: Jordan is death as ceasing to belong to this world at all, and entering into heavenly places, as belonging to them, with an ascended Christ. The Red Sea is death as redemption and deliverance, leading us to live to God in this world, and “if” remains. The Red Sea is deliverance into a responsible life in this world, though, if life be there, we shall reach the goal; Jordan is dying to it, and entering into Canaan as united to Christ.
paragraphs.source: J. N. Darby (‘Notes and Comments’. Vol. 2, p.143)

paragraphs.text: There were burnt offerings, meat offerings, peace offerings, and in each case the people were supposed to have something, a handful of meal if nothing more. There was a variety of gifts, so that the rich and the poor could each contribute. Mutuality is a great thought in Scripture; that is, that each one has part, either in contributing to what we are brought into or receiving of it.

God blesses each of us, the rain comes upon us all, and hence God looks for fruit, even from the very poorest spiritually, so that no one is shut out. “Unto every one of us is given grace according to the measure of the gift of Christ”, Ephesians 4: 7.

He (Abraham) nestled down under the protection of the faithfulness of God. He dwelt in Beersheba in the sense of the faithfulness of God. In his history there had been established a proverb, as I may say, “on the mount of Jehovah will be provided”. I can understand people saying to Abraham as he nestled there in Beersheba—‘Abraham, what about the possibility of famine? What about the winter that is coming? What about the education of your children?

What about the politics of the world, and how they may interfere with you?’. What would Abraham say to every such question? “On the mount of Jehovah will be provided”. That was his answer, that was his psalm. It became established in Israel. It was light for every believer afterwards to nestle in.
There is hardly anything that touches one more than the thought of the ark, the smallness of it and what it went through, and what it maintained—the full mind of God, and nothing lost.

My impression is that there is an immense amount of latent gift, a great deal of divinely given ability not exercised through different reasons. It is for every one of us to take that to heart and see to it that if there is ability it is exercised, and that we are good stewards of the manifold grace of God.
paragraphs.source: C. A. Coates (‘Outline of Luke’s Gospel’, p.164)

paragraphs.text: You cannot make a pony into a horse; but I insist on this, that the horse under a carriage is the same horse when under a cart. If he is a fine, well-stepped good-tempered horse under a carriage, he will be exactly the same under a cart. Are you to change because you are in adverse circumstances? A great man ennobles the lowest circumstances. In the common details of daily life, I am to manifest the power and beauty of the heavenly Man. “I can do all things through him who gives me power”. I derive entirely from Him. “The life which I now live in the flesh, I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me”. Trying circumstances are the very opportunity for you to display the greatness of His grace.

It has been said, ‘The expulsive power of a new affection’. I say, ‘The expulsive power of a new Person’. If a man could say he was the chosen friend of the sovereign, he would not want the company of others.
